---
title: "Get an overview of Zenodo deposits"
description: |
  Use the `list` command to retrieve all your Zenodo deposits and `get` to find a specific deposit.
order: 4
---

The `list` and `get` commands can be used to retrieve information about existing
Zenodo deposits on your own account. While `list` retrieves all deposits
associated with the authenticated Zenodo account, `get` finds the deposit in the
Zenodo account matching a specific `zendo_id` kept in the `.zenodo.toml` file.

Both commands are useful for checking whether a deposit already exists and
retrieving information about it before performing operations such as
[`update`](update.qmd) or [`publish`](publishing.qmd).

::: callout-note
<!-- TODO: Replace with an `includes` snippet for reuse across guides -->
zen-do authenticates your account using your Zenodo access token. If you don't
have one yet, you can create one by logging in to [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/)
or its [sandbox environment](https://sandbox.zenodo.org/).

Name your token `ZENODO_TOKEN` (for the production environment) or
`ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN` (for the sandbox environment), and store it in your
system keyring or as an environment variable.
:::

### Listing all deposits

The `list` command retrieve all deposits associated with your Zenodo account.

To list deposits in your Zenodo account, run:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
zen-do list
```

The optional `--sandbox` argument retrieves deposits from the Zenodo sandbox
website at [sandbox.zenodo.org](https://sandbox.zenodo.org) instead of the main
Zenodo website at [zenodo.org](https://zenodo.org):

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
zen-do list --sandbox
```

### Getting a specific deposit

While `list` will list *all* deposits in your account, the `get` command only
retrieves the Zenodo deposit JSON for a deposit in your account matching the
`zendo_id`. This ID is stored in the `.zenodo.toml` file. (Note: *In the Zenodo
deposit JSON, the `zendo-id` is found under `related_identifiers`*).

The command takes two optional arguments:

- The `--sandbox` as described above for `list` --- here, specifying a specific
  deposit.
- the path to the metadata file. If no path is provided, it defaults to
  `.zenodo.toml` in the working directory.

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
zen-do get path/to/.zenodo.toml --sandbox
```

The command searches all the deposits associated with your account (either the
sandbox or the main Zenodo website) and identifies a matching deposit using the
`zendo_id`. If a matching deposit is found, its deposit JSON is returned.

For example, to retrieve the deposit associated with the default `.zenodo.toml`
file, run:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
zen-do get
```

To search for the deposit in the Zenodo sandbox, run:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
zen-do get --sandbox
```
